title: BuildOS
caption: A project workspace you can talk to
eyebrow: From rough thought to working project
headline: The conversation becomes a place to work.
insight: BuildOS brings chat, tasks, documents, and project context into one workspace. Its public Fading Crown demo follows a fictional novel from rough description to a project with recent activity, milestones, and a suggested next move.

branches.title: A concrete first-use story
branches.description: The homepage demonstrates one recognizable book project across chat, task changes, and the resulting workspace.

branches.title: A useful place to return
branches.description: Recent activity, upcoming work, and project documents give the next session somewhere specific to begin.

branches.title: Product and identity together
branches.description: A warm paper surface, printed labels, and orange accents carry the same visual language from the public site into the application.

title: Chat into work
caption: Visible actions, inspectable results
headline: A reply can change the project—and show what changed.
insight: A request to move a writing block travels through real tools to a saved task. The chat presents tool activity and receipts, while the worker adapter reconciles durable messages and events when the browser reconnects.

branches.title: Receipts beside the conversation
branches.description: Tool results describe concrete project and entity changes, so a user can inspect the work behind the answer.

branches.title: Streaming with a durable record
branches.description: The interface separates temporary text previews from saved assistant text and deduplicates semantic events during reconciliation.

branches.title: Honest failure states
branches.description: Stop, reconnect, retry, and uncertain writes have dedicated handling instead of being flattened into a success message.

title: Connected work
caption: Goals, plans, tasks, documents
headline: The task keeps the context that makes it useful.
insight: BuildOS gives goals, plans, tasks, milestones, and documents their own editable surfaces and relationships. A task board sits alongside a document tree, with activity and document versions making changes inspectable over time.

branches.title: A working board
branches.description: Backlog, in-progress, scheduled, and overdue work are visible in the public demo, including the writing and beta-reader tasks from the conversation.

branches.title: Documents with history
branches.description: Document trees, version history, and comparison views support work that develops through revisions.

branches.title: Relationships are real data
branches.description: Mutation receipts verify the source, target, and project of a saved relationship, rather than treating links as decorative lines.

evidence: apps/web/src/lib/components/project/ProjectDocumentsSection.svelte: document tree and inherited document shelf

title: People & permissions
caption: Human access and agent access
headline: Invite the person. Decide what their agents can do.
insight: Project sharing distinguishes owner, editor, and viewer roles from a person's agent access. Invitations by email or handle, expiring links, and optional restricted project access make those boundaries visible in the interface.
steps: Invite by handle, email, or link
Choose a role and agent access

branches.title: Two separate decisions
branches.description: Agent access can be Off, Read, or Write. Write requires an editing role; the interface fits agent access to the selected human role.

branches.title: An invitation has a lifecycle
branches.description: Project invite links support 1-, 7-, or 30-day expiry, reset, turn-off, and QR display. Handles keep the underlying email private.

branches.title: A shared project still has an owner
branches.description: The collaboration surface includes member management, ownership handoff, notification preferences, and restrictions for external agents.

evidence: apps/web/src/lib/components/project/ProjectCollaborationModal.svelte: separate member and agent rights, ownership handoff, restricted access
apps/web/src/lib/components/project/ProjectInviteLinkPanel.svelte: invite-link expiry, reset, off, and QR display

title: Work that persists
caption: Worker lifecycle and integrations
headline: The browser is a window onto the work, not its lifetime.
insight: Worker-owned chat turns maintain execution identity, saved events, and recoverable state outside the browser. Separate background jobs handle calendar synchronization and briefs, while the Agent work surface organizes active work and history.

branches.title: Ownership with a heartbeat
branches.description: A worker renews a turn lease and stops acting when it loses ownership. Recovery and cancellation have explicit paths for failed or stopped work.

branches.title: External changes need receipts
branches.description: The mutation layer distinguishes confirmed results from uncertain writes; calendar jobs distinguish permanent failures from retryable responses.

branches.title: Useful integrations, visible work
branches.description: Calendar sync connects project events to scheduling. Brief jobs and the Agent work panel extend the workspace beyond a single conversation.

evidence: apps/web/src/lib/components/agent/agent-chat-worker-ui-adapter.ts: reconcile durable state and execution generations

title: Inkprint
caption: A visual language with meaning
headline: Paper, ink, and texture give the work a recognizable home.
insight: Inkprint defines warm paper and charcoal themes, orange signals, tactile surface weights, and textures with specific meanings. The same canonical stylesheet feeds a public design library, while a generator carries its theme into the mobile work in progress.

branches.title: Texture communicates intent
branches.description: Bloom signals ideation, Grain execution, Thread relationships, and Grid writable surfaces. The portfolio specimens reuse those source patterns.

branches.title: A bench with lighter sheets
branches.description: The app frame and page surfaces use different tones, crisp edges, and contact shadows to create hierarchy without heavy decoration.

branches.title: One source, multiple surfaces
branches.description: A sync script generates the public CSS library. Mobile theme generation is implemented; the native app is still in development.

evidence: apps/web/src/lib/styles/inkprint.css: canonical tokens, semantic textures, bench and sheet, weight system
status: Web design system; native app in development
